aspects.says: An abstract method overridden in each type puts the decision with the type: the most specific override runs, and a new class that lacks it does not compile.
basis: section:An instanceof Chain Fails Silently on a Subclass or a New Type; an Abstract Method Makes the Compiler Ask
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces has no wrong solution that compiles; the quiz's chain question checks the other side of the same trade

aspects.says: An instanceof chain runs its tests in order without any compiler check, so an early superclass test hides a subclass's branch and a new type falls into the default.
basis: section:An instanceof Chain Fails Silently on a Subclass or a New Type; an Abstract Method Makes the Compiler Ask

aspects.says: A List<Parcel> is not a List<Shipment>; a parameter read from is ? extends T and one written to is ? super T, each giving up the other direction, while arrays convert and fail at run time instead.
basis: section:A List of Parcels Is Not a List of Shipments; a Wildcard Says Whether the Method Reads or Writes

aspects.says: An accept written once in a base class, or inherited by a subclass, calls the overload for the class it is written in, so every class with its own overload needs its own accept.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: the accept Methods Look Duplicated

aspects.says: HotSpot inlines a call site that has seen one or two classes and compiles a virtual call once three or more reach it; the cost matters only for tiny methods in hot loops and is to be measured.
basis: section:A Call Site That Has Seen Three Classes Isn't Inlined, Which Matters Only in a Hot Loop

aspects.says: Java chooses the implementation from the receiver only and the overload from the arguments' declared types, so dispatching on a second object takes a second call: accept in each class, calling visit(this).
basis: section:Java Chooses the Method by the Receiver Alone, So Dispatching on a Second Object Takes Two Calls

aspects.says: When the types are fixed and the operations keep growing, or the types are not yours to edit, a switch over a sealed type is the better trade.
basis: section:An instanceof Chain Fails Silently on a Subclass or a New Type; an Abstract Method Makes the Compiler Ask
aspects.reason: a design trade-off with no behaviour to grade; unit 1.5.4 teaches and practises the switch
